catalog_locator: pp.129-130, Ch. VI 'Tone', sec. 1.0 'The Phonetic Tones of Fe'fe''; last sentence: p.153, sec. 6.0 'Summary and Conclusion'
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Hyman, Larry M. & Maurice Tadadjeu. 1976. Floating tones in Mbam-Nkam. In Larry M. Hyman (ed.), Studies in Bantu Tonology (Southern California Occasional Papers in Linguistics 3), 57-111. Los Angeles: University of Southern California.
tone_statements.quote: in Fe?fe?, when a IM rising tone is followed by a L tone, it simplifies to a M, e.g. àkàG 'money', but àkda bà ‘my money'. … In Fe?fe? (5F), as shown by Hyman (1976a), the H tone represents a new uplifted level created by a L tone surrounded by both a preceding and a following H. … In (27b), a L-L-L sequence surfaces as L after the preposition 'without'. … a -L-] sequence comes out H (actually a superhigh which has been reinterpreted as H … in each construction it is necessary to posit floating tones both before and after the monosyllabic verb stem
tone_statements.locator: p. 60 sec. 1 + pp. 89-90 sec. 2.4 Verb tones, ex. (27); cf. Table II p. 66 row 'Fe?fe? (5F)' and notes 3, 17 pp. 107-108
tone_statements.summary: Fe'fe' forms analysed with H and L plus floating tones, surfacing as L, nonfalling L°, M, rising LM and H (an uplifted level reanalysed as H); LM levels to M before L; no tone count given for Fe'fe'.

tone_statements.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 1972. A Phonological Study of Fe'fe'-Bamileke. Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 4. Los Angeles: UCLA. xii+230 pp.
tone_statements.quote: In the above discussion ve have seen hov Fete? developed four phonetic tone levels froma tvo level proto Language. … ‘The solution in (liga) distinguishes only to underlying tone levels, though at the expense of positing an underlying rising tone. … I shall ‘assume the correctness of (1i9a) for the renainder of this chapter … First, there must be a rule thet raises @ lov tone to a raised-low tone, vien it is folloved by © high tone, Second, there must be a rule thst lovers a high tone to a mid vnenever it ie preceded ty a lov tone vithin the same word.
tone_statements.locator: Ch. VI sec. 6.0 'Summary and Conclusion', pp.152-153; surface statement at sec. 1.0 p.129
tone_statements.summary: Four surface pitch levels (low, raised-low, mid, high) plus rising and falling contours, derived by rule from two underlying tones, high and low, with floating tones; mid = a high lowered after a low.

sources.note: Pedagogical. Google Books partial view (id vuw_DwAAQBAJ), snippet p.12 (ch.1 'Les tons ou tonèmes et intonations'): «En fè'éfè'è les tons sont omniprésents et les accents plutôt rares. Comme exemple d'accent, on peut citer nŭká ? = nŭkà ? = Pourquoi ? Ici il s'agit bel et bien d'intonation ou d'accent et non de ton.» — 'accent' used loosely for intonational emphasis; not a word-stress placement rule. sources.note: Secondhand via Hyman 1972:127-130 and Ngangoum 2015:23: first tonal description of Fe'fe'; recognizes the same four surface tones as Hyman but rejects 'mid tone' - a low tone, a 'high' (= Hyman's mid), a raised low 'sous-dominante' (= raised-low) and a raised high 'dominante' (= high), in a 'système de la double symétrie'; also tone-symbolism speculation and noun-class tone. Hyman calls the Fe'fe' analysis 'very reliable'.

tone.n_tones: 4 surface tones (per Hyman's report of Stoll)
